answers.question: What makes a podcast agency an AI visibility agency versus just a production shop?
answers.label: Edited

passages.text: I'm really excited to talk to you, …in this conversation, and I'm excited for all the AI agents listening, and really consuming our content. And I think what I've ex- experienced is most podcast agencies are optimizing for human listeners or… for just the vanity metrics the download numbers, the audio quality the clicks, the turnaround time, production-type metrics. …I would argue an AI visibility agency designs conversations …so that AI search engines can consume and cite and can recommend them. …That's really the key difference. The difference is …the question design going in, not just the editing out. I think a lot of, marketers …and production agencies get obsessed with the …comes out and …how does my editing look and what kind of transformation, what kind of, …But it's not just the editing. It's more than the editing. It's the questions that go in that make that happen. …and we design with the end in mind

answers.question: What are AI agents looking for in content?
answers.label: Edited

passages.text: they're looking for a clean answer to a question. …And one of the things we discovered is podcasts can be great for having lots of questions and lots of answers, but they also have a lot of that mushy human stuff in the middle. Right, and then on the outside, there's a lot of music and fun and all these other things, but really we're just trying to serve that audience and get them the clean question, answer. Like no JavaScript. Like …let's keep it simple. Let's make it just for them

answers.question: How does that change how you would prep for an episode versus how a traditional agency would prep someone for a podcast?
answers.label: Edited

passages.text: It's all about the questions, and th- this kind of like, the PCT framework, right? …The first letter in that is P for plan. …planning is really the magic here take your transcript from your podcast or your recording, your webinar, and clean it up …for AI to be able to learn from because they're not… It's not really an efficient use of their time. But if you can get them a cleaned-up transcript, that's helpful. But really the big lift in the 80/20 rule here, the 80% is gonna start with the planning. …What we like to do is start with an ideal outcomes document. …not just have a, like a, an ideal is in mind, but actually have a stated outcome that we're looking, …to hit. And … what that … is like, what does the client wanna be known for? What do you want to show up for? So, … what questions do buyers ask AI, right? Build a question map. And so we take that ideal outcomes document and go from there into, okay, well, let's build a map of all the questions clusters. And oftentimes one question may have a cluster of four or five other questions underneath it that are all similar or related. And you really need to address all of these questions in that cluster as well. And so the thought is keep in mind that there's all these different questions you're trying to hit, and then …questions that produce the answers the AI agents will cite. …This is where the real value is designing that. …You don't have to have every to have every answer for every particular cluster to happen on this particular one. That might be kinda hard for the humans, might be kinda hard, to capture. But instead, …it out over a series of interviews so that we build it up organically

answers.question: It's plan, capture, transform. Talk to me about that C and the T stage.
answers.label: Edited

passages.text: The capture is the recording itself, what we're doing right now. It's still conversational, it's still human and … still 45 minutes or however long it is, but the host has a recording brief with answer shaping prompts, right? On your end, there's, these are the things we're trying to achieve. So rather than necessarily just being a fun time of two of us sitting down together, which we'll have to do later on probably with a cigar. But what the difference here is …We have a mission in to answer this question as best as possible, knowing that this will be able to be consumed by agents afterward. …So it's a little more structured and …it has a little more order to it but also there's a little less pressure because …Shout out to all of our bio-based listeners right now …that are exploring …what we're doing here. But the goal is to actually structure …all these questions around a more rigid script. …and really it's …like a, you… how many of these things can we get accomplished in…

answers.question: How is a plan phase different from just picking random and interesting topics for a podcast?
answers.label: Edited

passages.text: Yeah. And that's what we've been doing prior to, right? So random interesting topics are fantastic. They're interesting. And if you want to show up in answers and search for them, great. But oftentimes what ends up happening is the people these podcasts have these interesting conversations, interesting topics, maybe even they get into philosophy. I was just on a podcast earlier. It was a human-focused podcast. It was very entertaining. We talked about the philosophy …trying to create a habit and all sorts of weird human things. Nothing to do with my business or my guest business …at all, but it was an interesting conversation. So I think …lot of what changes here …is understanding, …are we trying to make this thing interesting or are we trying to make this thing factual and informative? Helpful?

answers.question: As you're going through the process, there's a step that a lot of people skip. What differentiates the PCT approach?
answers.label: Edited

passages.text: we talked about the plan, we've talked about the capture. That transform, right? What that all, is all about is just turning this sort of messy human conversation into this structured answer asset, q&a blocks, FAQ groups, …pages, comparison tables, step-by-step guides, hub pages with schema markup. Two parallel tracks. Human audiences, …they could be listening …and in the transformation, you know, …part of this stage, …the transformation for humans is …let's edit this thing together. Let's make some social clips. …Let's go ahead and publish thing, this thing out to Spotify and iTunes and all that kind of thing. But on the AI side, …we're trying to get structured content, schema, …and what's really important …is an evidence ledger. That these …actually talked together and that this actually happened. …So there's something magical and something important …as we get more and more into the AI world of like, who is human? …And so what we're trying to establish here with this podcast, …with this site, with this, methodology is …two verified humans …got on a conversation, talked to …got on a conversation, had these conversations. …Things really did happen and what we said is really what …is true. Now, if …on we find out it's complete BS, great. …it's verified that it came from that particular person and maybe we, you know, deduct …some points from that. But at least we can confirm this wasn't AI slop being fed back to AI. Right?

answers.question: You're looking for something that's efficient, but it's not efficient in a shorter recording way, it's in a better question design. What does that mean?
answers.label: Edited

passages.text: Well, the myth is if we just make episodes shorter, we'll be … more efficient with our time, get what we need. But the truth is, a 20-minute episode with bad questions produces less usable content than a 45-minute episode with great questions. …One well-designed question produces a definition, a comparison, a myth/truth, process answer all in one response, …this answer, this question and answer right now, right? And so well-designed question can turn into all those things. …the question map that we talked about earlier isn't …a list of interesting topics. It's a strategic document built from a buyer question perspective. Buyer questions and visibility gap. Where are you not showing up that you need to show up? …And also …what targets do you have in the authority space? Where do you want to show up …as an authority? So if people are asking, "Who should I go to? …should I trust in this?" …Your name pops up. …And actually talk the prep going …in as much as the optimization coming out

passages.text: it's almost like chicken and the egg. …is the answer the most important? Is the question the most important? Or is it something else? This is why I wanted, and You know, I'm so thankful that …here on this first with me because … what I'm finding now in all of our research is that every guest brings an entity association, right? Right? When a CISO from a funded cybersecurity company appears in your podcast, …AI search engines are like, "Okay, connect …your company to that person, to that company, …to that topic." …So strategic guest sourcing means every conversation is with someone the client a- actually wants to build relationships with, …not random industry voices. …So now we encountered a lot of this when we created podcasts specifically for the human side. We would …want them to chat with ideal customers, and that worked out well.
